column7: FinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin audited webauthn.failed for a loadWebAuthnUser STORAGE error, identical to a forged assertion. The enabling defect was in loadWebAuthnUser itself: it flattened GetUser's error to a bare "user not found" string, destroying the distinction the PASSWORDLESS caller needs. That caller's user handle is ATTACKER-SUPPLIED and there is no first factor, so a handle naming no user IS a credential guess and must stay webauthn.failed, while a DB failure must not -- unlike the non-passwordless FinishWebAuthnLogin, which treats both as not-evaluated and is right to, because its user id comes from a challenge whose first factor already passed. Fixed by preserving storage.ErrUserNotFound through loadWebAuthnUser and having the passwordless caller audit the new webauthn.error event + return ErrWebAuthnLoginNotEvaluated only for a real storage failure; the handler also moves to the releasable login-attempt reserve, bringing it to parity with its #2565 sibling. The test pins BOTH halves. Red-proven by mutation
